To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Acanthamoebaprofilin binds to actin in a 1:1 stoichiometry with a Kd = 50 microM for Acanthamoebbactin and 150 microM for rabbit skeletal muscle actin.
the dissociation constants for the binding of Acanth amoeba profilin to Acanth amoeb a actin and skeletal muscle actin have been determined by direct physical measurement.
the profilin dissociation constants for Acanthamoebalabeled actins are Kd = (48 +/- 18) microM for actin from A. castellanii and Kd = (147 +/- 73) microM for rabbit skeletal muscle actin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of the actin-binding proteins with the actin filaments.
the physical characterization of the interactions between the actin monomer and the actin-binding proteins, which regulate actin polymerization.
the study of the interaction between actin and its binding proteins in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dissociation constants for Acanthamoebaprofilin binding to actin are 48 and 147 microM for Acanthamoeboae and rabbit skeletal muscle actin respectively.

, for the conditions used, the dissociation constants for Acanthamoebaprofilin binding to Acanthamoebinactin are 2.5-fold lower than for rabbit skeletal muscle profilin binding to rabbit skeletal muscle actin.

the dissociation constant K(d) of Acanthamobea profilin for Acanthamoebae actin is approximately 50 microM, with an error of about 30% in the determination of the absolute value of K(d), and that the diffusion coefficient of profilactin is about 6.7 X 10(-6) cm2 s-1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding constants for profilin to actin are not very sensitive to the source of the actin.
profilin binds to actin with a Kd of approximately 50 microM in the cytoplasm of Acanthamoeba castellanii and approximately 150 microM in the extracts of rabbit skeletal muscle.

the dissociation constants of profilin from both Acanthamoeban and rabbit skeletal muscle actins, determined by fluorescence recovery after photobleaching, are in the micromolar range and that profilin binding to actin does not alter the diffusion coefficient of the complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given profilin concentration, the amount of profilin bound to actin is much less than previously estimated from experiments using labeled actin.

the dissociation constant for the binding of Acanthamoea profilin to Acanthamoebae actin is about 10-fold higher than the dissociation constant of the corresponding interaction between rabbit skeletal muscle profilin and rabbit skeletal muscle actin.
the fluorescence photobleaching technique can be used to obtain reliable estimates of the dissociation constants of profilins from a wide variety of sources to fluorescently labeled actins.
